candidate.title: NSCR
candidate.scope: The NSCR (nascent strand capture and release) row of the assigned Illumina schematic, from an RNA-primed replication bubble through short-strand selection, 5′ biotin capture, RNase I release, and amplification to DNA. The far-left bubble is an assay overview icon. Bubble-Seq above, Repli Seq below, clipped neighboring captions and the right-hand chemical legend are context, not alternative NSCR workflows. Primary sources clarify this depicted SNS implementation; unshown applications and library-preparation steps are outside the graph. The selected short-strand size class and RNA-dependent release define the origin-mapping implementation here; the papers’ unshown Okazaki-fragment or ribonucleotide-mapping applications do not add targets. A shared capture/release schematic does not assert identical complete implementations across the two papers.

states.label: Genomic DNA containing a replication bubble and RNA-primed nascent DNA
features: Parental genomic DNA and a nascent strand are shown within a replication bubble.
The consequential nascent-strand structure is a 5′ RNA leader covalently joined to DNA.

evidence.locator: NSCR row, DNA replication bubble and purple RNA primer label
[b00010], Results: Identification of DNA replication origins by NSCR
evidence.quote: The NSCR method is based on a positive selection for the ∼12-nt RNA leader that is introduced at the 5′ end of nascent strand DNA by primase activity during the initiation of DNA replication.

states.label: Size-selected single-stranded gDNA and SNS mixture
features: Denatured broken genomic DNA and short nascent strands remain mixed.
SNS carries its 5′ RNA primer; size selection alone does not identify nascent DNA.

The primary Figure 1 defines the selected SNS size class as approximately 400–2000 nt, chosen to avoid shorter Okazaki fragments and retain DNA near origins; these bounds are not printed in the Illumina drawing.

features: The physical readout carrier is amplified genomic DNA derived from released SNS; its genomic distribution can localize regions of replication initiation.

operations.label: Denaturation and size-selection
operations.description: Denature replication-containing genomic DNA and select short single-stranded material, producing a mixture of SNS and similarly sized broken genomic DNA.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper identifies heat denaturation and sucrose-gradient size fractionation. At this scope, the combined depicted block recovers short strands with their RNA leaders intact; its selected size class is chosen to avoid shorter Okazaki fragments while retaining origin-proximal DNA.
operations.information_effect: Retains origin-proximal SNS along with size-matched background DNA; selection is not yet specific for the RNA-DNA chimera.

operations.label: 5′-biotinylation
operations.description: Attach a 5′ biotin handle to both the genomic DNA fragments and the RNA-DNA nascent strands.
operations.mechanism: The diagram combines end labelling into one block. Primary Figure 1A identifies 5′ thiophosphate installation followed by chemical modification with biotinylated maleimide. On SNS this labels the RNA end, creating an attachment path that can later be broken by RNA cleavage.
operations.information_effect: Creates attachment competence without distinguishing SNS from broken gDNA.

operations.label: Streptavidin pull-down
operations.description: Immobilize the biotinylated mixture on streptavidin support; both gDNA and RNA-DNA SNS are captured. The pale short strands above the support are unlabelled free material; their chemical identity and downstream fate are not assigned by the drawing.
operations.mechanism: Biotin-streptavidin binding changes the molecules from free to support-bound.
operations.information_effect: Retains the DNA portions of SNS through their 5′ RNA leaders; affinity capture alone does not select origins.

[b00192], Figure 1 caption
evidence.quote: The pooled fractions will contain both nascent strands and broken DNA (black lines), both of which are 5′ biotinylated (indicated with B).

operations.label: RNase I digestion
operations.description: Cleave the RNA segment connecting the 5′ biotin attachment to nascent DNA. Nascent DNA becomes free while nonreleased gDNA and biotin-linked RNA remnants remain on the support.
operations.mechanism: RNase I digestion of the RNA leader breaks the attachment path to the downstream DNA. RNase I is a reagent acting on the captured substrate, not a material output.
operations.information_effect: Enriches DNA by RNA-dependent release from captured molecules. The physical criterion is cleavable RNA between attachment and DNA; incorporated ribonucleotides can also enable release, so recovered DNA is not guaranteed to derive exclusively from initiation-associated SNS.

operations.label: Isolate and amplify SNS
operations.description: Collect the RNase I-released DNA fraction and amplify it to give the terminal DNA product; retained support is not routed into the product.
operations.mechanism: The primary protocol identifies whole-genome amplification of the RNase I release fraction; its internal stages are not decomposed by this schematic.
operations.information_effect: Amplified genomic sequences are the readout carrier for localizing origin-proximal SNS enrichment and comparing replication-origin usage after sequencing. WGA can truncate products, erase native SNS orientation and bias genomic representation. Thus the product supports regional enrichment, without preserving native SNS endpoints or guaranteeing an unbiased count of initiation events. The drawing ends at DNA; adapter-library construction, sequencing and mapping are not separate depicted operations.

evidence.quote: WGA results in truncation and loss of 5′ to 3′ orientation relative to the initial NSCR isolated SNSs. checks.rationale: The PubMed title/identifiers identify PMID 26949711, DOI 10.14440/jbm.2015.92, as the NSCR protocol. The independently checked collection heading and reference match that title. Full-text experimental-design paragraphs and Figure 1 caption directly support the declared SNS capture/release architecture and amplification interface, so content_checked/supports_architecture is justified for NSCR. This is distinguished from the poster’s literal Genome Research citation; metadata alone is not used as chemistry verification.
